'''Ghulam Murtaza''' (born 3 January 1939), {{small|[[Sitara-e-Imtiaz|SI]], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]}}, is a Pakistani [[theoretical physicist]] with a specialization in the [[Plasma physics|physics of ionized plasmas]], and is an [[Emeritus Professor]] of physics at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] in [[Lahore]]. Murtaza's work is recognizable in plasma physics and controlled nuclear fusion processes to provide a better understanding of energy propagated by the [[main-sequence star]], the [[Sun]].{{rp|1–2}}<ref name="Springer, Rawat, 2017">{{cite book |last1=Rawat |first1=Rajdeep Singh |title=Plasma Science and Technology for Emerging Economies: An AAAPT Experience |date=2017 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-981-10-4217-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6to4DwAAQBAJ&dq=ghulam+murtaza+plasma&pg=PA1 |access-date=8 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

From 2000 till 2020, Murtaza served on the science faculty of the Government College University where he directed the [[Abdus Salam Chair in Physics]].<ref name="GCU Press, 2020">{{cite web |title=A farewell ceremony for Ghulam Murtaza |url=http://gcu.edu.pk/abdus-salam-chair-in-physics/#1583907289698-9977fefd-e705 |website=GCU Press |access-date=8 May 2020 |language=en-us |date=3 March 2020 |archive-date=30 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200530174101/http://gcu.edu.pk/abdus-salam-chair-in-physics/#1583907289698-9977fefd-e705 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ICTP - Salam Chair, 2000">{{cite web |last1=ICTP |first1=ICTP |title=ICTP - Salam Chair |url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2000/4/salam-chair.aspx# |website=ictp.it |publisher=ICTP Press |access-date=8 May 2020 |location=Trieste, Italy |language=en-uk |date=1 April 2000 }}</ref>

==Biography==

Ghulam Murtaza was born in [[Amritsar]], [[Punjab, British India|Punjab]] in the [[British Indian Empire]] on 3 January 1939, and was educated in [[Lahore]].<ref name="PAS Fellow">{{cite web |title=Pakistan Academy of Science {{!}} Fellow Profile |url=https://www.paspk.org/fellow-profile/?fellowID=51 |website=www.paspk.org |access-date=8 May 2020}}</ref> Murtaza attended the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] (GCU) in Lahore where he graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) in physics in 1958– his graduation was noted when he was awarded the [[Honors student|Roll of Honour]] during the ceremony.<ref name="PAS Fellow"/> He then entered the [[University of Punjab, Lahore|Punjab University]] in Lahore and graduated with a [[Master of Arts]] (MA) in mathematics, and left for the [[United Kingdom]] in 1960.<ref name="PAS Fellow"/> He attended the [[London University]] in England, and graduated with [[Master of Science]] (MSc) in physics within a year before moving to attend the [[Imperial College London]] on financial funding sponsored by the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC).{{rp|ii}}<ref name="G. Murtaza, Imperial College, 1966"/>

Murtaza joined Dr. [[Abdus Salam]]'s doctoral group with Dr. [[P. T. Matthews]] where he engaged in research on [[elementary particles]].{{rp|157}}<ref>{{cite book |title=International Physics & Astronomy Directory |date=1969 |publisher=W. A. Benjamin |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SYzvAAAAMAAJ&q=ghulam%20murtaza |access-date=8 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 1966, Murtaza defended his thesis on elementary particles, written under the joint supervision of Abdus Salam and P. T. Matthews, and was conferred a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) in [[theoretical physics]], and a [[Diploma of Imperial College]] (DIC) from Imperial College in London.<ref name="G. Murtaza, Imperial College, 1966">{{cite web |last1=Murtaza |first1=Ghulam |title=Some Topics in Elementary Particle Physics |url=https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/bitstream/10044/1/17457/2/Murtaza-G-1966-PhD-Thesis.pdf |publisher=Imperial College London |access-date=8 May 2020 |location=London, UK |pages=149 |language=en-uk|year=1966 }}</ref> His thesis, "''Some Topics in Elementary Particle Physics'', focused towards discussing topics in [[Nuclear decay|decaying state]] in excited elementary particles and [[Lagrangian mechanics]] introduced in the concepts of [[symmetry in quantum mechanics]].{{rp|104–137}}<ref name="G. Murtaza, Imperial College, 1966"/>

===Academia and professorship===

In 1960, Murtaza instructed courses in mathematics as a lecturer at the [[University of the Punjab, Lahore|Punjab University]] till 1962 when he found employment with the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) as a scientific officer.<ref name="PAS Fellow" /> Upon return to Pakistan in 1966, Murtaza joined the natural science faculty at the [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] where he taught physics till 1999. During this time, Murtaza served as Chairman of the [[Institute of Theoretical Physics, Qau|Institute of Theoretical Physics]] twice, and later Dean of the Natural Science Faculty from 1996 to 1999.<ref name="PAS Fellow" />

In 2000, Murtaza left [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] to join the GCU Lahore and established the [[Abdus Salam Chair in Physics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ICTP - Salam Chair |url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2000/4/salam-chair.aspx |website=ictp.it |publisher=ICTP Salam Chair |access-date=9 May 2020 |location=Trieste, Italy |language=en-uk |date=1 April 2000 }}</ref> In 2004, Murtaza became the director of the [[Abdus Salam School of Mathematical Sciences|National Center for Mathematics]] at the GCU Lahore until 2006.<ref name="PAS Fellow" /> In 2007, Murtaza later took over the Salam Chair in Physics which he continued to led till 2020, and is now [[Emeritus Professor]] of physics at the Government College University.<ref name="GCU Press, 2020"/><ref name=" Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation">{{Cite web |author=COMSTECH |author-link=COMSTECH |title=Dr. Ghulam Murtaza |website=comstech.org |publisher=Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation |url=http://comstech.org/leading/Physics.pdf}}{{dead link|date=October 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission and research===

In 1962, Murtaza joined the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) as a scientific officer, and was a senior scientific officer when he left his research position at the PAEC in 1969 to join academia.<ref name="PAS Fellow" /> At PAEC, he collaborated with the Laser Physics Group under Dr. [[Shaukat Hameed Khan]], a laser physicist.<ref name="Rehman, Printwise publications, 1999"/> His research was originally focused towards understanding [[elementary particles]] but became interested in controlled [[thermonuclear fusion]] at the [[Quaid-i-Azam University]], and was a participant in early efforts in the mathematical calculations regarding [[nuclear fission]] energy during [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|Pakistan's atomic bomb program]] started in 1972.{{rp|17}}<ref name="Rehman, Printwise publications, 1999">{{cite book |last1=Rehman |first1=Shahid-Ur |title=Long road to Chagai |date=1999 |publisher=Printwise Publications |location=Lahore, Punj, Pakistan |isbn=9789698500009 |pages=157 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sNMgAQAAIAAJ&q=ghulam%20murtaza%20 |access-date=9 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

However, his interest in understanding nuclear fission led him to conduct research in controlled thermonuclear fusion, and he was a founding director of the Fusion Laboratory at the Quaid-i-Azam University.{{rp|587}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Panarella |first1=E. |title=Current Trends in International Fusion Research |date=2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4615-5867-5 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yKTaBwAAQBAJ&dq=Ghulam+Murtaza+fusion&pg=PA587 |access-date=9 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> His further research in plasma physics was conducted at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in 1990s, which he remained associated with in successive years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Physics in Pakistan |url=https://portal.ictp.it/pio/words/newsletter/backissues/News_94/features_Pakistan.html |website=portal.ictp.it |access-date=9 May 2020 |date=1 May 1994}}</ref>

In his country, Murtaza conducted pioneering research in topics in [[plasma physics]], and published papers in that field in respected international journals.{{rp|41}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Murtaza |first1=Ghluam |title=Effective Lagrangian in pion-production process |date=1970 |publisher=Oak Ridge Directed Operations, Technical Information Division |location=US |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6A46AQAAMAAJ&dq=Ghulam+Murtaza+fusion&pg=PA41 |language=en}}</ref> In 2007–08, Murtaza joined PAEC as the director of the National [[Tokamak fusion]] Program, and oversaw the commissioning of the [[GLAST (tokamak)|GLAss Spherical Tokamak]] (GLAST) at the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] (PINSTECH).<ref>{{cite web |title=33 International Nathiagali Summer College on Physics and Contemporary Needs, 23 June - 5 July, 2008, Nathiagali, Pakistan |url=https://media.nti.org/pdfs/21_11.pdf |website=nti.org |publisher=NTI |access-date=9 May 2020}}</ref>

===Recognition===

Murtaza is an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] which he was elected to in 1983, a [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences]], elected in 1991, and a recipient of the [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]] in 1996, and the [[Khwarizmi International Award]] in 1997.<ref name="PAS Fellow" />

==Scientific papers and publications==
* Radiative Collapse in an impurity-seeded spinning gas-puff staged pinch, Plasma Physics, (Arshad M. Mirza, Zahoor Ahmad, N.A.D Khattak, G Murtaza)
* Study of Plasma Parameters in a Spinning Thick-Gas-Puff Staged Pinch, Plasma Physics, Arshad M. Mirza, Zahoor Ahmad, N.A.D Khattak, G. Murtaza.
* Impulsion Dynamics of a Dense q-Pinch Plasma Driven by Multicascade Linear System, Laser and Particle Beams, G. Murtaza, Zahoor Ahmad.
* Magenetohydrodynamic (MHD) Model for the Staged Pinch Plasma to Study Fusion Parameters and Comparison with Snow Plow Model, Physics of Plasma, Ghulam Murtaza.
* Thermonuclear Fusion with Multicascade Linear Staged Pinch Plasma and Mechanics, Ghulam Murtaza.
* Study of Fusion Parameters in Multicascade Linear System, Dr. Zahoor Ahmad, G. Murtaza, N.A.D Khattak.
* Light cone algebra in various (1974), Fortschritte der Physik, Volume 22, Ghulam Murtaza
* Three-dimensional solitons, Physical Review, (1979) by M.Z.Iqbal and [[A H Nayyar|A.H. Nayyar]], G. Murtaza
* Nonlinear destabilisation, Fluid Physics (1985) Volume 28, P.K.Shukla and M.Y. Yu, G. Murtaza
* New electron temperature-graduate, Fluid Physics (1989), P.K. Shukla and G. Murtaza
* Electron Thermal Conduction for nuclear radiation, Volume 33 (1991), Arshad M. Mirza, C. L. Cook, G. Murtaza and M.S.Qaisar.
* Duality of a young diagram in Linear Geometry (1973), Mathematical. Physics Journal, M.A. Rashid and G. Murtaza
* Electromagnetic instability in Plasmas, Physics of Plasmas (1996), Arshad M. Mirza, G. Murtaza and P.K. Shukl.
* Longitudinal oscillations and simple gravity pendulum, Physical Review (2003), N. A. D. Khattak, G. Murtaza and H. A. Shah
* Some electrostatic modes based on Plasmas and radiations, Physics of Plasmas (2004), S. Zaheer, G. Murtaza and H. A. Shah
* [http://www.ncp.edu.pk/docs/12th_rgdocs/G-Murtaza.pdf Adiabatic model for dust atoms and molecules] by Ghulam Murtaza, Z. Ehsan, N. L. Tsintsadze, Abdus Salam National Center for Mathematics and Salam Chair in Physics, GCU Lahore, Pakistan
